text.p: Italy's debt market closed around the day's highs with Btp futures storming up after a slow start, boosted by the dollar's strength sending the lira to a high against the mark under 970 not seen since January.

"The bond markets just don't want to come down. The dollar's strength this afternoon allowed the September Btp contract to recover from what looked like a downturn until the afternoon," one trader said, noting Bund futures were also at day highs.
The September Liffe Btp contract ended 54 basis points up at 136.78 after a high at 136.79 and low at 136.33.
The Btp future rose even further in Liffe APT trade.
The dollar on Friday touched a near six-year high versus the mark at 1.7703 marks. The lira touched 969.60 per mark, its highest since January this year.

"I don't see any reason why the futures should ease," one trader said, adding that in the absence of any bad news on the single European currency front there was every reason to buy Btps. "No one wants to risk being left short in this market because they could really get hurt," another said.
Traders saw very strong support for the Btp at 136.00.
On the cash market, the February 2007 Btp gained 40 bps to 102.75, yielding 6.45 percent, with the 10-year Btp/Bund spread steady at a low 91 basis points.

"With the Bund so strong it will be difficult to see the spread narrowing below 90 bps. The future can rise some more but I think the spread is at its low for the moment," one trader said. But another trader was more optimistic:
"Underlying sentiment is still very positive and in this scenario the spread could narrow to 80 bps by the end of next week with the September Btp at 139.00," he said.
